intro: China is a different problem from the United States, and it is worth being blunt about why. Your VX-6R transmits on 144–148, 222–225 and 430–450 MHz. China allocates 144–146 and 430–440 MHz to amateurs, so the radio is capable — but the channels you would use in America are outside China's allocations and illegal there. Meanwhile China's licence-free walkie-talkie band sits at 409 MHz, which the VX-6R cannot transmit on at all. So there are exactly two honest paths: get a Chinese amateur licence and a compliant radio, or buy a pair of 409 MHz consumer radios. Both are covered below.
introz: 中国的情况和美国完全不同，值得直说原因。VX-6R 的发射频段是 144–148、222–225 和 430–450 MHz；中国划给业余业务的是 144–146 和 430–440 MHz，所以硬件是够用的——但你在美国用的那些频率都落在中国的划分之外，在国内属于违规。另一方面，中国的免执照对讲机频段在 409 MHz，而 VX-6R 根本无法在那里发射。所以实际上只有两条诚实可行的路：考中国业余电台执照并使用合规设备，或者买一对 409 MHz 民用对讲机。下面两条都写清楚了。
warn: Two separate requirements apply in China. First, transmitting on amateur bands needs a Chinese 业余电台操作证书 plus a station licence — a foreign licence is not automatically valid. Second, every transmitter used in China needs SRRC 型号核准 (type approval), and a US-market VX-6R does not have it. Receiving is a different matter and is not generally restricted, but forwarding or publishing the content of other people's communications can be. Treat the VX-6 as a receiver in China unless you have sorted out both the licence and the equipment.
warnz: 在中国有两个彼此独立的要求。第一，在业余频段发射需要中国的《业余电台操作证书》和电台执照，境外执照并不自动有效。第二，在中国境内使用的任何发射设备都需要 SRRC 型号核准，而美版 VX-6R 并没有。收听是另一回事，通常不受限制，但转发或公开他人通信内容则可能违法。除非执照和设备两件事都已解决，在国内请把 VX-6 当作接收机使用。

stations.n: 公众对讲机 Ch 1 — licence-free, anyone may use
stations.z: 公众对讲机 1 频道 · 免执照
stations.d: China's licence-free band is 409.7500–409.9875 MHz: twenty channels at 12.5 kHz spacing, 0.5 W maximum, integral antenna only, no licence and no registration. Realistic range is several hundred metres in a city and a few kilometres with line of sight. Channel 1 is the factory default on nearly every cheap radio, which makes it the worst choice — see the next entry.
stations.dz: 中国的免执照频段是 409.7500–409.9875 MHz：20 个信道，间隔 12.5 kHz，最大 0.5 瓦，只能用原装天线，无需执照也无需登记。实际距离在城市里几百米，视野开阔时几公里。1 频道是几乎所有廉价电台的出厂默认值，因此是最差的选择——见下一条。

stations.d: Near the top of the band. Because consumer radios default to the low channels and most people never change them, the last few channels are consistently the quietest. Add a DCS code and you will effectively never hear a stranger. This is the channel to actually use.
stations.dz: 接近频段顶端。民用电台默认停在低信道，而大多数人从不修改，所以最后几个信道一直是最安静的。再加一个 DCS 码，基本不会听到陌生人。这才是真正应该用的信道。

stations.d: The last channel in the band. Same DCS code as your primary so switching needs no discussion.
stations.dz: 频段最后一个信道。DCS 码与主频相同，切换时不需要多说一句话。

stations.z: VX-6 无法在此频段发射
stations.d: 409 MHz falls outside the VX-6R's transmit blocks, so for licence-free use in China you need a type-approved 409 MHz radio. They are inexpensive and sold everywhere. Your VX-6 can still monitor the band, which is genuinely useful for hearing what channels are busy before you pick one.
stations.dz: 409 MHz 不在 VX-6R 的发射频段内，所以在国内做免执照通信必须另买一台过了型号核准的 409 MHz 电台，价格便宜、随处有售。VX-6 仍然可以监听这个频段——在选择信道之前先听听哪些信道忙，其实很有用。

stations.d: China follows the IARU Region 3 band plan, where the FM simplex segment runs roughly 145.200–145.575 MHz with 145.500 as the calling channel. Sitting at 145.250 keeps you clear of both the calling frequency and the repeater sub-bands. Confirm the current plan with the local 无线电协会 — regional practice varies more in China than in the US.
stations.dz: 中国遵循 IARU 第三区频段规划，FM 直通段大致在 145.200–145.575 MHz，其中 145.500 为呼叫频率。选在 145.250 既避开呼叫频率，也避开中继台子频段。请向当地无线电协会确认当前规划——中国各地的实际做法差异比美国大。

stations.z: FM 呼叫频率（IARU 三区）· 请勿占用
stations.d: The equivalent of America's 146.520. Monitor it, call on it, do not camp on it.
stations.dz: 相当于美国的 146.520。可以守听、可以呼叫，但不要长期占用。

stations.z: APRS 数据（一区与三区）· 严禁语音
stations.d: Note this differs from the American APRS frequency of 144.390. If you carry one channel plan between countries, this is exactly the kind of detail that catches people out.
stations.dz: 注意这与美国的 APRS 频率 144.390 不同。如果你想把一套频率方案两国通用，这正是最容易出错的地方。

stations.n: 70 cm — usable but check locally first
stations.z: 70 厘米 · 可用，但请先在当地核实
stations.d: China's 70 cm allocation is 430–440 MHz. The widely used convention is repeater outputs around 439 MHz with inputs 5 MHz lower around 434 MHz, so a simplex channel here risks sitting on top of a repeater. Ask locally before settling on anything in this band.
stations.dz: 中国的 70 厘米划分是 430–440 MHz。普遍的惯例是中继台下行在 439 MHz 附近、上行低 5 MHz 在 434 MHz 附近，所以在这里开直通有可能压住某个中继。在这个波段定频之前，先问当地。

stations.n: 433 MHz — avoid, this band is full of noise
stations.z: 433 MHz · 避免，这一段噪声极大
stations.d: 433.050–434.790 MHz is China's short-range device band: car key fobs, doorbells, tyre-pressure sensors, weather stations, cheap remote controls. It is the single noisiest stretch of UHF in the country and no place for a conversation, even though the band plan nominally permits FM simplex there.
stations.dz: 433.050–434.790 MHz 是中国的短距离设备频段：车钥匙、门铃、胎压传感器、气象站、各种廉价遥控。这是国内 UHF 里噪声最大的一段，完全不适合通话——尽管频段规划名义上允许在此开 FM 直通。

stations.n: American channels do not work here
stations.z: 美国的频率在国内不能用
stations.a: Do not carry these across the border
stations.d: China's 2 m allocation stops at 146.000 MHz, so every American 2 m simplex channel — 146.460, 146.520, 146.550, 147.480, 147.540 — is outside the band in China. Likewise 446 MHz is above China's 440 MHz limit, and 1.25 m is not an amateur band in China at all. Build two separate memory banks and label them, rather than trying to find one set that works in both countries. There isn't one.
stations.dz: 中国的 2 米划分到 146.000 MHz 为止，所以美国那些 2 米直通频率——146.460、146.520、146.550、147.480、147.540——在国内全部超出频段。同理，446 MHz 高于中国 440 MHz 的上限，而 1.25 米在中国根本不是业余频段。建议直接建两组独立的存储分区并标注清楚，不要指望找到一套两国通用的频率——不存在。

stations.n: 1.25 m is not allocated in China
stations.z: 1.25 米在中国未划分给业余业务
stations.a: Do not carry these across the border
stations.d: The band that makes your VX-6 special in America is unavailable in China. Do not transmit there.
stations.dz: 让 VX-6 在美国显得特别的那个波段，在中国无法使用。请不要在此发射。

stations.n: Hong Kong and Macau are separate jurisdictions
stations.z: 香港与澳门属独立管理辖区
stations.a: Do not carry these across the border
stations.d: Hong Kong licenses amateurs through its own authority with its own callsign series and reciprocal arrangements that differ from the mainland's. If you plan to operate in the Greater Bay Area, treat crossing the boundary as changing countries.
stations.dz: 香港由本地主管部门独立发放业余电台执照，有自己的呼号序列，互认安排也与内地不同。如果计划在大湾区活动，请把过境视为换了一个国家。

stations.n: A workable protocol for a group
stations.d: Primary channel, one backup, one DCS code, and an agreed rule: if you lose contact, go to the backup, and if that fails, go back to the primary and wait on a five-minute cycle. Write the two channels on a piece of tape on the back of each radio. Everything else is optional. Note that DCS and CTCSS only keep your squelch closed — they are not encryption, and anyone scanning will still hear you.
stations.dz: 一个主频、一个备频、一个 DCS 码，再加一条约定：失联就切备频，备频也不行就回到主频，按五分钟为周期等待。把这两个频率写在胶带上贴到每台电台背面。其余都是可选项。要注意 DCS 和 CTCSS 只是让你的静噪保持关闭——它们不是加密，任何在扫频的人都能听到你们。
